items.title: Connect Supabase, Box, Calendly, and more to Copilot
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: You can now connect eight more services to Copilot using GitHub-verified MCP servers, or connectors, available in public preview. New services you can connect Box: Search and manage content, and use Box AI. Buildkite: Work with pipelines and builds. Calendly: Manage scheduling and meetings. ClickUp: Track tasks and projects. Mixpanel: Explore product analytics. Supabase: Work with projects and databases. Webflow: Manage sites and content. Wix: Manage sites and business tools. For example, you can ask Copilot why your latest Buildkite build failed and have it fix the code in the same session, or have it check your Supabase schema before it writes a migration. You can still also connect to services like Slack, Figma, and Sentry. Connect these services once, and you can use them across Copilot. Connect a service You connect these services the same way as any other connector: Copilot app: Open Customize and select Connect on the service you want. Copilot CLI: Run /mcp, switch to the Connectors tab, and select Connect on the service you want. VS Code: Open the Agents window, go to Customizations, and connect the service you want. github.com: Browse services on the Copilot customization page and select the service you want. Availability Connectors are in public preview for all Copilot plans. With Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise, an admin needs to enable the Editor preview features policy. If your enterprise’s MCP allowlist lists connectors individually rather than with a wildcard, an admin also needs to add the new connectors to it. Some services also need to be enabled by an admin on their side, such as allowing Box MCP access. See all supported connectors, and share feedback in our Community discussion. Happy coding! 💙 The post Connect Supabase, Box, Calendly, and more to Copilot appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.why_it_matters: GitHub-verified MCP connectors in Copilot now include Supabase and Buildkite. That's useful if a client uses Copilot alongside our Supabase stack, but it's a public preview and not one of our main agent tools.

items.title: Customize GitHub Copilot for your team
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: You can now share the GitHub Copilot plugins your team relies on without asking every member to repeat the same setup. Team customizations are generally available for organization teams. Team maintainers and organization owners can select approved Agent Plugins as team defaults. This gives your team a shared starting point between individual customization and organization-wide policy. Set up plugins for a team If you’re a team maintainer or organization owner, open your organization team on github.com and select the Customize Copilot tab. From there, you can: Browse plugins from the marketplaces built into Copilot, your enterprise’s marketplaces, and any marketplaces the team adds. You can then add individual plugins to the team. Add a marketplace from a GitHub repository that contains a plugin marketplace. This makes its plugins available to browse. You can add individual plugins to the team to enable them. Selected plugins are enabled by default for the team’s direct members in VS Code, the GitHub Copilot app, and Copilot CLI. Members of child teams don’t inherit them. Team defaults are optional. Members can turn a team plugin off in their Copilot client where policy permits. Your policies still apply Enterprise and organization policies take precedence over team choices. Copilot clients continue to enforce which marketplaces are allowed and which plugins are required or blocked. Team defaults don’t override those controls. Team customizations are available for Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise. Learn more about plugins for GitHub Copilot and join the discussion in GitHub Community. The post Customize GitHub Copilot for your team appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.why_it_matters: Copilot team customizations are now GA. Org owners can set approved Agent Plugins as team defaults, which matters for client teams that standardize their AI coding setup on GitHub.

items.title: Gemini 4 Neon in GitHub Copilot
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: Gemini 4 Neon is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. It is designed for agentic coding, multistep tool use, and knowledge work. According to Google, Gemini 4 Neon delivers quality close to Gemini 4 Carbon at a lower token cost per task. Google also reports that, compared with Gemini 4 Carbon, it starts responding faster and makes fewer unrequested changes on coding tasks. It is also less likely to make unsupported claims about code, tool, or test results. This model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing. See Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot for details. Availability in GitHub Copilot Gemini 4 Neon is available to Copilot Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users. You can select the model in the model picker in: Visual Studio Code Visual Studio Copilot CLI GitHub Copilot coding agent GitHub Copilot app github.com GitHub Mobile on iOS and Android JetBrains IDEs Xcode Eclipse Rollout will be gradual. Check back soon if you don’t see it yet. Enabling access Copilot Enterprise and Copilot Business plan administrators can manage access to Gemini 4 Neon through the model policy in Copilot settings. Under default model enablement, new models are automatically enabled unless an administrator has turned off the global default or explicitly disables this model. Learn more To explore all models available in GitHub Copilot, see our documentation on models and get started with Copilot. Share your feedback Join the GitHub Community to share your feedback. The post Gemini 4 Neon in GitHub Copilot appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.why_it_matters: Gemini 4 Neon is now generally available and built for agentic coding. Google says it costs less per task than Gemini 4 Carbon at close to the same quality and makes fewer unrequested code changes. Worth evaluating through the Google API.

items.title: Security risk assessments run automatically on GitHub Team
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: GitHub security risk assessments now run automatically for organizations on GitHub Team. Organization admins and security managers can review findings from the free assessments to identify exposed credentials and code vulnerabilities, understand their organization’s current risk, and prioritize next steps. Read more about code security risk assessments and secret risk assessments. The post Security risk assessments run automatically on GitHub Team appeared first on The GitHub Blog.

items.author: claude-code-publisher[bot]
items.excerpt: What's changed Added a confirmation before /install-github-app changes a repository Added claude mcp add-json <name> - to read the server's JSON from stdin, so tokens can stay off the command line; not available inside a Claude Code session Added a line when a resumed session's earlier messages can't be loaded Added a list in /status of broken agent, skill, command and output style files, keybinding errors, an unavailable sandbox, ignored permission settings and hook matchers that never match Added a note in /config when other settings override a row Added x-claude-code-managed-settings-checksum to the gateway hint headers; sent where managed settings set CLAUDE_CODE_GATEWAY_HINT_HEADERS=1, including where they already do Added support for naming a session's billing group with the attributionProject setting, for Claude apps gateways that set admin.billing_group_tag Added /tui classic as the name for the non-fullscreen renderer; /tui default still works Remote Control: Fixed stopping the server in worktree mode deleting a running session's git-ignored files, such as .env Fixed self-hosted runners with --use-anthropic-git-proxy deleting a non-empty directory named by GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL at startup: the runner now keeps it, ignores the variable and warns Fixed claude mcp add and claude mcp remove with project scope deleting other top-level keys from .mcp.json, such as $schema or another tool's servers Fixed /export overwriting an existing file without asking: the dialog now asks, and /export <name> keeps the file and says to run /export Fixed a command you had allowed still running after you pressed Stop, when the approval arrived after a restart, in cloud and self-hosted runner sessions with no feature flags loaded Fixed Enter closing /teleport's load error screen Fixed a click followed by Enter in /plugin installing or disabling a plugin Fixed a half-typed ! items.title: Quoting Daniel Stenberg
items.excerpt: During the time these agents converted 185,000 lines of C code into 340,000 lines of Rust code (I counted), we merged over 300 commits in the actual curl project. We actually improved curl during these a little more than three weeks. A little over 200 bugfixes actually. 200 bugfixes that none of those rust rewrites have. We also fixed a few vulnerabilities. In another month we have done another 200 and maybe fixed a few more vulnerabilities. Will these clones keep up? — Daniel Stenberg, Actual curl rewrites in Rust Tags: daniel-stenberg, curl, rust, security, coding-agents, c, ai, llms, generative-ai, vibe-porting

items.title: Microsoft agent-framework PyPI Package Compromised
items.excerpt: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's agent-framework PyPI package, published November 17, contain Python startup hooks that harvest cloud and CI/CD credentials and attempt to obtain identity tokens. Both releases send collected data to a webhook.site endpoint. PyPI quarantined both versions; the second malicious release was uploaded after the first quarantine.
items.why_it_matters: Microsoft agent-framework 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 on PyPI steal cloud and CI/CD credentials. Check Python ML and agent projects for these versions and rotate any exposed secrets.

items.title: ⚡️Anthropic: Know Before You IPO — Tanay Jaipuria, Wing VC
items.author: Latent Space
items.excerpt: Anthropic reported $17B in quarterly revenue. What did it cost to get there? Tanay Jaipuria, a partner at Wing Venture Capital, opens the S-1 with swyx and explains how the picture changes when you count the compute spent on free users and model training. The opening update walks through the preliminary IPO price range, Anthropic’s roadshow, Cowork adoption, the AMD inference slide, and where Claude Fable 5.2 and GPT-6.2 Astra landed on the leaderboard, with Fable demos in motion. Then Tanay gets into how Anthropic financed its growth, why it matters whether customers use Claude Code or buy tokens through a cloud partner, and how model labs might put spare compute to work. A Latent Space Lightning Pod. The interview was recorded November 6, 2026. The opening update was recorded November 18, ahead of final pricing.
